correctness.rationale: When e/gcd(e,ell) is odd in characteristic two, gcd(2^ell+1,2^e-1)=1, so every Lagrange coefficient has a unique (2^ell+1)-st root. Substituting these roots into the GRL Galois-dual equations and scaling z=k-s-h multipliers forces g=f^(2^ell), then forces the top s coefficients of f and z evaluation values to vanish, leaving exactly h degrees of freedom. The converse is direct, and finite generator-matrix checks agree with the formula.

originality.rationale: The motivating GRL hull paper assumes 2ell|e and its common arbitrary-hull construction requires normalized Lagrange coefficients to lie in a specified subfield. Wan--Zhu already cover the odd-quotient characteristic-two regime for GRS/EGRS codes, so neither that regime nor the power-map lemma is claimed as new. Targeted literature searches found no prior arbitrary-evaluation, arbitrary-extension-matrix GRL theorem in this regime. The claim is restricted to this GRL consequence and its distance-neutral hull tuning; priority risk remains elevated because the motivating preprint is recent.

value.rationale: The result removes evaluation-set and subfield restrictions for an infinite characteristic-two parameter regime, including cases ell does not divide e, and shows that every fixed GRL distance skeleton in the stated range can realize all hull dimensions 0,...,k-s. Since multiplier changes are diagonal Hamming isometries, prescribed hull tuning is separated from the classical distance design problem.
